title: Quantization run custodian: orchestration, artifact lifecycle, retention and access model for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: High-level summary of intended orchestration for calibration runs in Redwood Console covering FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. Focus on run lifecycle, artifact provenance, TTL/retention policies, role-based access and validation hooks. Goal is to provide operators and platform users with a predictable, auditable pipeline that integrates with console rollouts and Dedicated/Private deployments.
spec: 1) Run lifecycle states: Scheduled -> Running -> Succeeded/Failed -> Archived. 2) Each run emits immutable artifacts: profile.json (quant params), calibration_trace.tar.gz (KV samples + metrics), accuracy_report.html, raw_eval_logs.ndjson. 3) Artifact metadata must include run_id, model_version, dataset_hash, seed, hardware_profile, quant_backend, and checksums. 4) Retention policy: default 90 days for full artifacts, 365 days for profile.json, configurable per-org with min retention 7 days, max 3 years. 5) Access model: roles -> Viewer (read artifacts metadata), Operator (trigger/stop runs, read artifacts), Custodian (modify retention, delete after TTL), Auditor (read only, exportable). 6) Deletion workflow: soft-delete, quarantine window 14 days, final purge requires Custodian or automated scheduled gc respecting org policy. 7) Validation hooks: post-run accuracy validator that compares baseline metrics and tags regression if drop > configured threshold; optional manual approval step before promoting quant-profile to runtime catalog.
acceptance_criteria: - Console UI lists runs with clear state and duration, expandable to artifact list. - Artifact download links are signed and expire per org config. - Retention settings available at org and project level with overrides and effective retention shown. - RBAC enforced on run actions and artifact access; e2e tests demonstrate Viewer cannot delete artifacts. - Post-run validator triggers and emits alert when accuracy regression detected; alerts link to failing artifacts. - GC job purges eligible artifacts and records audit events.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: longer retention increases S3 cost; recommended org default 90 days balances reproducibility and cost. Consider tiered retention: short TTL for raw traces, longer for distilled profiles. We need SSO-integrated audit events to satisfy compliance customers. Edge-case: runs created from private deployments must respect on-prem storage constraints and may disable GC.
